extracted.intended_audience: technologists, scientists, engineers, and other experts from industry and academia interested in serving as PETTP guest lecturers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for external experts who want to present technical training to USPTO patent examiners through the Patent Examiner Technical Training Program (PETTP). Covers eligibility, content expectations, logistics, and policy constraints for presentations and related stakeholder programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide relevant, historic and current technical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest lecturers provide relevant, historic and current technical knowledge, including industry practices/standards in technological areas of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should reflect the state of the art and be useful to patent examiners; see 'list of topics' for areas of interest. Presentations should focus on technical knowledge rather than case-specific legal argument or application advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lecturer qualifications — relevant technical knowledge and industry practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest lecturers must also have relevant technical knowledge and industry practices/standards in areas of technologies where such lectures would be beneficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers should be practitioners or researchers with demonstrable technical expertise in the topic area so examiners receive authoritative, current industry/technical perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format and locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guest lecturers have the option of presenting a lecture in-person or virtually from their own location. In-person presentations can be made at our Alexandria, Virginia headquarters or at one of our regional offices in Dallas, TX, Denver, CO, Detroit, MI and San Jose, CA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training delivered at each location will be broadcast to patent examiners across the entire USPTO. Choose format and location that support broad examiner access; virtual presentations are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation — no discussion of pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: PETTP is not intended as an opportunity for applicants to discuss pending applications with USPTO employees or to circumvent normal communication between applicants or applicants' representatives and USPTO employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use PETTP as a channel for application-specific advocacy or to bypass established prosecution channels. Content should avoid referencing or analyzing pending filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No advice or recommendations to the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: PETTP participants are not to provide advice or recommendations to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentations should be informational/educational only; avoid advising USPTO policy or procedures. Clarify that the role is to educate examiners on technology, not to consult for the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invited Speaker Consent Form required
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to giving a presentation, all PETTP guest lectures must sign the USPTO's Invited Speaker Consent Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the consent form is completed and returned before presenting. Preferably, presentations are recorded and made available to employees for later viewing or listening—check consent form for recording permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests evaluated on resources, time, and topic appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to serve as a PETTP guest lecturer are granted depending upon resources, training time available, and appropriateness of the topic suggested. For granted requests, audience size will vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting an interest form does not guarantee participation; select and prioritize topics that match examiner needs and available scheduling/resources. Be prepared for variable audience sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit interest form and align with Technology Center topics
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are interested in participating as a guest lecturer, please submit an interest form. Scheduled 2025 Tech Fairs for each Technology Center are provided; please see list of topics that may be of interest to examiners. Additional topics may be proposed by guest volunteer lecturers and considered for presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing topics, consult the Technology Center topic list and tailor proposals to examiner interests. Use the official interest form to apply; you may propose additional relevant topics for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology Center topic alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: PETTP Technology Fairs are organized by Technology Center (e.g., 1600 Biotechnology and organic chemistry; 2100 Computer architecture and software; 2800 Semiconductors, memory, optics...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your lecture topic maps to the Technology Center descriptions and audience. The Technology Center list provides examples of acceptable subject areas and helps target the correct examiner audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site Experience Education (SEE) hosting requirements and funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Site Experience Education program provides commercial, industrial, and academic institutions, within the continental U.S., the opportunity to voluntarily host patent examiner technical site visits. The USPTO funds all SEE travel costs for patent examiner visits to host organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host organizations must be within the continental U.S. and volunteer to host site visits; USPTO covers travel. SEE is a separate but related program for hands-on site-based examiner education.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEPP — stakeholder training derived from examiner training material
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stakeholder Training on Examination Practice and Procedure program offers those interested training opportunities to better their understanding of the examination process at the USPTO. Training material used is derived from material developed for training patent examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STEPP sessions adapt examiner-training content for external stakeholders; presenters/participants should expect materials oriented to explaining examination practice and procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: SOaR program offerings for stakeholder education
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOaR program offers interactive online courses, in-depth topic discussions, legal and CLE trainings, expanded trainings for non-professional (pro se) applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOaR is an avenue for broader stakeholder education; offerings include CLE and materials targeted to pro se applicants. Contact SOaR@uspto.gov to learn how to attend or propose sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings and dissemination preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferably, PETTP presentations are recorded and made available to employees for viewing or listening at a later time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan presentations with recording in mind and confirm permissions via the Invited Speaker Consent Form; recorded materials extend training reach across the USPTO.
